title: 📰 AI news · October 23

items.title: Railway asks users to rotate all keys
items.text: Railway says an outsider may have reached the settings that hold project keys and passwords, and for some users saw them decrypted. If your bot or site runs on Railway, your keys live in exactly those settings. Rotate your keys and passwords today and check the logs for unusual sign-ins.

items.title: Malware slipped into the LiteLLM library
items.text: Attackers hijacked the release of the popular Python library LiteLLM and published version 1.107.0, which steals cloud passwords and AI keys. It was live on PyPI for about 1 hour 45 minutes. If your project talks to AI models, check your LiteLLM version; if it is 1.107.0, roll back to 1.106.2 and rotate your keys. Free guide «Code Protection in One Prompt» — send the word «protect» to the bot.

items.title: Hackers attack companies with an AI agent
items.text: Microsoft described ARTEX, an AI-agent toolkit a Chinese group used against ConnectWise. The agent made up to 2,900 sign-in attempts a minute against accounts at more than 2,250 organizations. If you run a bot or service with password sign-in, turn on two-factor protection and limit login attempts.

items.title: Capcom: 11.7M player emails leaked
items.text: Through the CAPCOM ID service, email addresses, sign-in dates and IP addresses got out. Other players' passwords and card data were not affected. If you store customer emails, check who has access to that database.

items.title: 1Password: AI signs in without your password
items.text: The new 1Password for Agents lets agents sign in to services while you approve each login and the agent never sees the password. It works with Claude Duet, ChatGPT Work, Grok Bot and Muse. If you connect an agent to your accounts, pick a way where the password stays in your password manager.

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Duet
items.text: The new agent app for everyday work runs on Claude Opus 5.5 and connects to more than 6,000 services. It is a preview for Pro and Max subscribers with a waitlist, and payments need your approval.

items.title: OpenAI opens the Decisions API
items.text: The model makes decisions in 100–180 milliseconds instead of 1–3 seconds. It is now open to all OpenAI customers. For agent services that means faster replies.

items.title: Canva releases Canva Craft
items.text: Canva's first in-house image model plans the layout and text first, then draws an image up to 2K in one of 30 aspect ratios. It is available to everyone in the Dream Lab tab and through the API.

items.title: Nirva: a pendant that listens only to you
items.text: The device weighs about 8 grams, lasts up to three days and filters out other voices using a sample of yours. Orders open in November at $249.

items.title: Spotify gets ready for AI agents
items.text: Spotify was the first music service on Meta's Muse assistant and also works with ChatGPT and Claude. It does not pass listener data to partners: the agent asks for music and Spotify decides what plays.

takeaway: Three stories today are about keys and access: Railway, LiteLLM and an AI-agent attack. Recommendation: find where your bot's keys are stored and replace the ones you haven't changed in a while.
